correctness.rationale: Independence and domination are encoded exactly by no adjacent 11, no triple 000, and endpoint 00 restrictions; a three-state transfer has the specified initial and terminal vectors. The alternating seven-sign product maps the terminal vector to its negative. Padovan-count parity is seven-periodic modulo two by the recurrence and three initial values. Seeds at n=2,3,5 plus repeated seven-sign blocks give zeros in every even-count residue class. Convolution invertibility follows from standard Walsh diagonalization; brute-force independent checks are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The main assertion is a universal all-frequency Walsh nonvanishing theorem for maximal-independent-set indicators on paths. Known Padovan counts give only a parity obstruction; they do not construct zero coefficients when the count is even. The exact seven-sign transfer identity and constructive seeded witnesses resolve this missing direction. Searches and selected full-text inspections below found no equivalent or stronger theorem. Historical priority is bounded, not guaranteed.

value.rationale: The complete zero-free classification of a canonical graph-defined convolution operator answers a precise spectral question for every dimension. Ordinary counting only supplies a parity obstruction; a nontrivial transfer antisymmetry closes the other direction constructively. The exact modulus-seven phenomenon and its dimension-independent seven-sign identity identify a structural constraint of the independent-domination language, beyond a small finite computation or a routine restatement of its Padovan cardinality.
